verses.text: Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD: "I will sing to the LORD, because he has won a glorious victory. He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea.
The LORD is my strength and my song. He has saved me. He is my God, and I will praise him. He is my father's God, and I will lift him up high.
The LORD is a warrior. The LORD is his name.
He has thrown Pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea. Pharaoh's best officers drowned in the Red Sea.
The deep waters covered them. They sank to the bottom like a stone.
Your right hand, LORD, is glorious in power. Your right hand, LORD, smashed the enemy to pieces.
In your great majesty you threw down those who rose up against you. You sent out your burning anger, and it burned them up like dry straw.
With a blast from your nose the waters piled up. The flowing waters stood up like a wall. The deep waters became solid in the middle of the sea.
The enemy said, 'I will chase them and catch them. I will divide what I take from them. I will take all I want. I will pull out my sword, and my hand will destroy them.'
But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who among the gods is like you, LORD? Who is like you, glorious in holiness, amazing in praises, doing wonders?
You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
In your faithful love you will lead the people you have set free. In your strength you will guide them to your holy home.
The nations will hear and shake with fear. Terror will grip the people of Philistia.
The leaders of Edom will be afraid. The strong men of Moab will tremble. All the people of Canaan will lose their courage.
Terror and fear will fall on them. Because of the power of your arm they will be as still as a stone, until your people pass by, LORD, until the people you bought pass by.
You will bring them in and plant them on your own mountain, the place, LORD, you made for your home, the holy place, Lord, that your hands have built.
The LORD will rule forever and ever."
When Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the people of Israel walked through the sea on dry ground.
Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her, playing tambourines and dancing.
Miriam sang to them: "Sing to the LORD, because he has won a glorious victory. He has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea."
Then Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea, and they went into the desert of Shur. For three days they travelled in the desert without finding water.
When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. That is why the place is called Marah, which means bitter.
So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we going to drink?"
Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD gave them a rule and a law, and there he tested them.

He said, "If you listen carefully to the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his laws, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD, who heals you."
Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there near the water.
